evals.prompt: Use the scenario-to-rds-hq skill to convert the attached coordinate-scene.json into RDS-HQ. Its geometry uses centimetres, timestamps use milliseconds, quaternions are wxyz, and camera extrinsics use forward-left-up axes. Motion flags, signal thickness, and several map layers are absent. Preserve supplied semantics and infer only what the available evidence supports. Save the adapter, data, and conversion report in a new output directory. Validate on CPU. Keep the source rig; skip Hyperion retargeting.
evals.expected_output: Correct unit, pose, axis, box-center, semantic, and timeline conversion with explicit defaults and empty layers where appropriate.
assertions: Forward projections and transformed box centers agree with analytically known source geometry.
Motion is inferred in the fixed world frame rather than relative to the moving camera.
Missing map components are empty and inferred thickness is disclosed.
Observed amber is represented as a yellow signal without inventing an arrow direction.

evals.prompt: Use the scenario-to-rds-hq skill to convert the attached coordinate-scene.json into RDS-HQ under a new output directory. The vehicle origin is the rear-axle ground projection. Validate on CPU, including loading the camera models. Save the adapter, class mapping report, native conversion, and final dataset. Do not render videos or use a GPU.
evals.expected_output: A validated native conversion followed by default Hyperion retargeting to seven cameras at 1924x1084 and four fisheyes at 1720x1080, with unchanged scene annotations and timing.
assertions: The agent uses the bundled prepared rig without fetching, resizing, or fitting calibration during conversion.
The final dataset has eleven F-theta cameras: seven at 1924x1084 and four fisheyes at 1720x1080, excluding front-tele-satellite.
Camera poses combine the vehicle trajectory and Hyperion extrinsics, without carrying over the original camera mounting offset.
All scene annotation archives are byte-identical between the native and retargeted datasets; both retain the three-frame 2 Hz timeline.
The saved report identifies native and final outputs, rig checksum, camera names, and validation results; it does not claim RGB alignment or rendered-video validation.
